organizations.active_dates: Established as a Maryland National Guard training camp in 1926; opened in 1927; federal wartime use began in 1942.
organizations.normalization_notes: The historical Camp Albert C. Ritchie name is preserved. Fort Ritchie is retained as a later alias. The camp was a Maryland National Guard installation; no modern successor relationship is inferred.

affiliations.occupation: Self-taught architect and engineer; military officer
affiliations.date_precision: Western Maryland Historical Library dates Barrick's appointment to take charge of the camp to 1926. The Ritchie History Museum describes his post-engineer and superintendent service as continuing through World War II; an exact end date and OSS transition date are not established.
affiliations.research_notes: The assignment is definitely documented before and during the wartime period, but the reviewed sources do not state when or how Barrick entered OSS-related service. It is therefore not labeled immediate pre-OSS. It is a military assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Raymond J. Barriault is high-confidence matched to the Hudson, New Hampshire veteran publicly identified with OSS in 2007.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A university-hosted campaign document lists the rare name Raymond Barriault of Hudson with OSS; a separate Hudson obituary index supplies the same middle initial as the NARA row.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare exact first and last name, the matching J middle initial in the Hudson obituary index, Hudson residence, explicit OSS designation, and an age-compatible 2009 obituary. The indexed grade and private identifier remain unmatched externally.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish wartime OSS identification and later Hudson residence but do not document service dates, recruitment chronology, occupation, or employer.
claims.match_notes: The match remains high confidence rather than confirmed pending Box 39 and identifier comparison. No employment inference is drawn from residence or veteran status.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Robert F. Barrick is high-confidence matched to Maryland National Guard officer and Camp Ritchie engineer Robert Frederick Barrick.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Official state preservation records and two regional historical institutions identify Robert Frederick Barrick as the Maryland National Guard officer who designed, built, and supervised Camp Ritchie.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact Robert F. Barrick name, full middle-name expansion, commissioned military status, and the unusually specific wartime intelligence-installation connection. The private index identifier and Box 39 file remain unreviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: Institutional sources place Barrick at Camp Ritchie from 1926 through World War II, but do not directly describe his OSS entry or duties.
claims.match_notes: The identity remains high confidence rather than confirmed until Box 39 or an identifier-linked official record establishes direct personnel-file linkage.
